Hello, a birth is expected for {cow} in {herd} on {due}, in {days_to_due} days. Please move the animal to the maternity pen and check her often as the date comes near.
Hello, {subject} in {herd} is being treated for {cause} with {medicine} for {days} days. Please keep it apart from the group, give it water and tell me if it gets worse.
Hello, {vaccine} for {herd} is planned for {planned}. Please prepare the handling area for {head} animals and write the batch number and the animals vaccinated.
Hello, {qty_kg} kg of {feed} for {herd} is due on {due}. Please clear space in the store and check the weight and the date on the delivery note.
Hello, please weigh {subject} in {herd} today ({n_weighed} animals) and send me the average weight by the evening.
Hello, please move {herd} to {paddock} on {in_date} for {days} days. Check the fence and the water before the move and count the animals after it.
Hello, {count} animals were lost in {house} on {date}, cause: {cause}. Please check the other animals, remove the dead ones and send me a short report.
Hello, a water trough fault was reported in {house} for {herd}. Please repair it today so that the animals can drink, and tell me when it is done.
Hello, the ration of {herd} changes: {feed} is now {kg} kg as fed per head per day. Please use the new amounts from the next feed.
Hello, the withdrawal period of {subject} in {herd} ({medicine}) ends on {free_date}. Please do not sell milk or meat before that day.
Hello, the order of {qty_kg} kg of {feed} for {herd} covers about {cover_days} days. Please plan the next order so that the group never runs short.
Hello, {tag} in {herd} is on the cull list for {date}, reason: {reason}. Please prepare the animal for sale and check that it is not under a withdrawal period.
Hello, the pregnancy check of {cow} in {herd} shows: {result}. The birth check says: {state}. Please update the breeding plan.
Hello, we booked your visit to {herd} on {date} for {purpose}. We will have the animals and the handling area ready. Please confirm the time.
Hello, please confirm the treatment plan for {subject} in {herd}: cause {cause}, medicine {medicine}, {days} days. Tell me if you want a recheck.
Hello, we would like a pregnancy scan for {cow} in {herd}. Please tell me your first free day this week and how many animals you can scan.
Hello, please order {name} for the next vaccination round. We have {stock} {unit} left and the expiry is {expiry}. Please send the price and the delivery day.
Hello, we lost {count} animals in {house} on {date}. Please do a post-mortem and send the result so that we can protect the rest of the group.
Hello, we order {qty_kg} kg of {feed} for {herd}. Please deliver on {due} and send the weighbridge ticket with the delivery.
Hello, order {fb_id} of {feed} is due on {due}. We may need it earlier. Can you deliver sooner or tell me the new day?
Hello, we need {name}. Stock is {stock} {unit} and the reorder level is {reorder}. Please send a quote, the expiry date of the batch and the delivery day.
Hello, we need bedding for {herd}: {qty_kg} kg of {feed} on {due}. Please tell me the truck size and the arrival time.
Hello, please book shearing for {name}, about {head} animals, on {next_work}. Tell me the size of your team and your price per animal.
Hello, please repair the fence in {paddock} ({area_ha} ha) before {in_date}, because {herd} moves in on that day. Tell me when you can come.
Hello, please watch {cow} in {herd} for signs of heat around {repeat_date}. If she is in heat, tell me at once so that we can serve her again.
Hello, please check the temperature, the air and the water in {house} now. There are {head} animals inside and the space check shows: {state}.
Hello, {qty} animals ({subject}) from {herd} are ready for collection on {date}. Please confirm the truck and the time of arrival.
Hello, transport is booked for {qty} animals ({subject}) of {herd} on {date}. Please give water, stop feeding in time, check the tags and prepare the movement papers.
Hello {visitor}, you visit {herd} on {date}. Please disinfect your boots and your vehicle {vehicle} at the gate, wear the clean overalls we give you and sign the visitors log.
Hello {keeper}, herd work for {name} is planned on {next_work} for {head} animals. Please prepare the handling area, the records and the helpers.
Ear tag: {col:animals.tag}. Group: {col:animals.herd}. Species: {col:animals.species}. Breed: {col:animals.breed}. Sex: {col:animals.sex}.
Born on {col:animals.born}, which makes the animal {col:animals.age_m} months old. The dam is {col:animals.dam}. The status is {col:animals.status}.
The last weight was {col:animals.last_kg} kg on {col:animals.last_date}. The animal had {col:animals.treatments} treatments in the last 12 months. Withdrawal check: {col:animals.wh_state}.
This passport goes with the animal when it is sold or moved and is kept with the herd records.

The group started the records with {col:herds.opening} animals. {col:herds.came} came in and {col:herds.left} left, so there are {col:herds.head} animals now, which is {col:herds.units} livestock units.

The ration is {col:herds.ration_kg} kg as fed for each animal and costs {col:herds.feed_head} per head per day. The average daily gain is {col:herds.adg} kg. {col:herds.deaths} animals died in the last 12 months, a rate of {col:herds.mort_rate}. The check shows: {col:herds.mort_state}.
Animals in treatment now: {col:herds.sick}. Vaccinations overdue: {col:herds.vacc_late}. The next herd work is planned for {col:herds.next_work}.

The vaccine was planned for {col:vacc.planned} and given on {col:vacc.done_on} by {col:vacc.vaccinator}. {col:vacc.doses} doses were used for a group of {col:vacc.head} animals, a coverage of {col:vacc.coverage}.
The vaccination is repeated after {col:vacc.interval_days} days, so the next one is due on {col:vacc.next_plan}. The status shows: {col:vacc.state}.
Please keep the batch number and the expiry date of the vaccine with this certificate.
Treatment and withdrawal record of {set:firm}, dated {today}.

The treatment started on {col:withdraw.treat_date} and lasted {col:withdraw.days} days. The withholding period is {col:withdraw.milk_days} days for milk and {col:withdraw.meat_days} days for meat, plus {set:wh_extra} safety day.

Milk may be sold from {col:withdraw.milk_free} and meat from {col:withdraw.meat_free}. The animal is free from {col:withdraw.free_date}. Status: {col:withdraw.state}. Checked by {col:withdraw.checked_by}.
Do not deliver milk or send the animal for slaughter before the free date. Keep this record for inspection.
Animal: {col:breeding.cow} in {col:breeding.herd}. Service on {col:breeding.date} by {col:breeding.method}, sire {col:breeding.sire}, done by {col:breeding.done_by}.
With a gestation of {col:breeding.gest} days the birth is due on {col:breeding.due}. If the service failed, the animal returns to heat on {col:breeding.repeat_date}.
The result of the service shows: {col:breeding.state}. The pregnancy check is made {set:preg_check_days} days after the service.
The keeper moves the animal to the maternity pen two weeks before the due date and calls the vet if a birth does not progress.
Feed ration statement of a group
Group: {col:herds.name}, {col:herds.head} animals with an average weight of {col:herds.avg_kg} kg.

The ration is {col:herds.ration_kg} kg as fed for each animal per day. It gives {col:herds.dm_pct} of the body weight as dry matter. The cost is {col:herds.feed_head} per head per day, or {col:herds.feed_day} for the whole group.
For each kilogram of gain the group eats {col:herds.fcr} kg of feed at an average daily gain of {col:herds.adg} kg.
Any change of ration is written here and signed by the livestock manager before the next feed.

Buyer, seller or source: {col:moves.party}, phone {col:moves.party_phone}. Total live weight {col:moves.weight_kg} kg, which is {col:moves.kg_head} kg per head. Value {col:moves.value}, {col:moves.price_head} per head.
The animals are fit to travel and are not under a withdrawal period. The driver confirms that the animals were loaded calmly and that the vehicle was clean.
The cause is recorded as {col:mortality.cause}. This is {col:mortality.share} of the group and the value lost is {col:mortality.value}.
The keeper checked the other animals, removed the dead animals as the law requires and told the vet. A post-mortem result will be added to this report when it arrives.
Livestock stock list for the bank

There are {col:herds.head} animals with an average weight of {col:herds.avg_kg} kg, which is {col:herds.units} livestock units. The value per head is {col:herds.value_head} and the value of the group is {col:herds.stock_value}.
The values are the farm estimate at the date above. Animals are counted from the movement records and checked against the register.

Open Start and type your farm name and your own limits in the yellow cells: the grazing area, the yearly mortality you accept, the days of warning and the safety days for withdrawal.
List your groups on Herds and Flocks with species, house, keeper, standards and the head at the start. The head now updates from Animal Movements.
Record every ear tag on Animal Register. Weights, treatments and the withdrawal status of each animal fill in.
Enter services on Breeding and scans on Pregnancy Checks. The due date, the return to heat and the result of each service fill in, and births go on Births.
Weigh animals or batches and write them on Weights and Growth. Daily gain is checked against the target of the group.
Plan vaccinations on Vaccination Schedule and write the day each one was given. Overdue and due soon warnings appear by themselves.
Write each treatment on Treatments. The Withdrawal Tracker shows the days left before milk and meat can be sold. Keep medicines on Medicine Stock.
Write the feeds of each ration on Feed Rations, orders on Feed Purchases and weekly use on Feed Use to see cost per head and days of feed.
Use Grazing Rotation, Housing and Pens, Mortality, Culling List and Biosecurity Visitors for the daily running of the farm.

Use the 14 calculators for ration cost, feed needed, feed conversion, daily gain, due dates, heat, withdrawal, stocking rate, dry matter, mortality, replacements, vaccine doses, grazing days and water.
Print 10 sheets and 9 letters, follow 10 checklists and tap a message link to open WhatsApp with the text ready.
Read Livestock Dashboard and Charts every week: head, births, feed days, withdrawals, vaccinations and losses.
Track milk, eggs, harvest lots, stock and traceability in one file
Milk, eggs, harvest lots, stock, cold rooms and traceability
every dispatch is matched to its harvest lot, field and date, and a check flags lots with no record and loads larger than the lot
each load gets a lot number with field, crop, tonnes and moisture, and shows the tonnes sent to buyers and the tonnes left
fat, protein, cell count and tank temperature of every milking are checked, and each pickup shows the buyer result and the paid litres
tonnes in, out and corrected give the signed balance and value of every product, and a count shows the difference against the book
Bins and silos with moisture checks
capacity, fill, moisture and inspection dates show which bin is nearly full, too wet or due for a check
Cold chain with the range of each room
every reading is compared with the range of its own cold room, store or milk tank and flagged too warm, too cold or too humid
Egg lay rate and cracked share
hen-day lay rate and cracked eggs per section and day are compared with your targets, and grading shows packed eggs, dozens and value
live and carcass weights give the dressing percentage of every batch against its target, with weights per animal and value
moisture before and after, fuel and hours give the tonnes after drying, the water removed and the cost per tonne
Storage loss by cause and value
each loss is priced from your price list and ranked by cause, product and month against the loss you accept
all costs for a product divided by what you produced give the cost of a litre, dozen, kg or tonne against its price
Crates and pallets that came back
quantity out and back per buyer shows what is missing, its deposit value and the days out

One row for each milking with litres, fat, protein, cell count and tank temperature; litres per cow and a quality check against your limits fill in.
One row for each pickup with litres, fat, protein, cell count, bacteria and the price; the result of the buyer test, the paid litres and the value fill in.
Egg collection per day and house section
One row for each collection with hens in lay, eggs and cracked eggs; the lay rate, the cracked share, good eggs and a check against your targets fill in.
Egg grading and packing for buyers
One row for each grade and week with eggs graded, downgraded eggs, buyer and price per dozen; packed eggs, dozens, trays and the value fill in.
Meat records: live weight, carcass and dressing percentage
One row for each slaughter batch with animals, live weight, carcass weight and price; dressing percentage, weights per animal, value and a check fill in.
Wool and fleece clips by grade
One row for each grade of a clip with the animal group, fleece weight, price and buyer; the value and the number of bags fill in.
Harvest lots: one number for every load that goes into store
One row for each lot with field, crop, tonnes, moisture and store; tonnes sent to buyers, tonnes left, the link to a buyer and the moisture check fill in.
Grain bins and silos: capacity, content and moisture
One row for each bin or silo with capacity, content, moisture and the date of the last inspection; the fill, space left, moisture, inspection check and value fill in.
Cold rooms, stores and tanks with their temperature range
One row for each cold room, store or tank with stock, the temperature range it must hold and the reading now; the check, days since the last check and value fill in.
Stock movements: every tonne in, out and corrected
One row for each movement with product, tonnes, store and the lot or note; the signed tonnes and the value of the movement fill in.
Stock count against the book and the difference
One row for each product counted with the tonnes you count; the book stock from the movements, the difference in tonnes, share and value, and a check fill in.
Drying and cleaning log with fuel and cost
One row for each drying, cleaning or sorting job with tonnes, moisture before and after, fuel and hours; tonnes after drying, water removed, cost per tonne and a check fill in.
One row for each reading of a cold room with temperature and humidity; the range of the room and a check against it fill in.
Storage losses and spoilage by cause
One row for each loss with product, cause, tonnes, store and lot; the value lost and the size of the loss fill in.
Packing and grading of fresh produce by quality class
One row for each packing run with product, class, crates, crate weight, rejects and buyer; net weight, tonnes, reject share, value and a check fill in.
Crate and pallet tracking: what went out and what came back
One row for each dispatch of crates, pallets or bins with the quantity out and back and the deposit; the missing quantity, its value, days out and a check fill in.
Lot to buyer traceability: from field to buyer
One row for each dispatch with the lot number, buyer, tonnes and delivery note; field, crop, harvest date, days in store and a traceability check fill in from the lot.
One row for each product and quality class with the specification and the price per tonne; the price against Class 1 fills in, and the stock values in this file use these prices.
Quality complaints and returns from buyers
One row for each complaint with buyer, lot, cause, tonnes affected and the claim; days open, value of the goods, claim share and a reply check fill in.
Cost per unit produced for every product
One row for each product with the quantity produced, its costs this year and its price; total cost, cost per unit, margin per unit and a check fill in.

Herd supervisor: milk tank too warm
Hello {keeper}, the milk tank read {tank_temp} degrees C on {date} after the {grp} milking. Please check the cooling, the thermostat and the cover now and tell me what you find.
Hello {keeper}, the cell count for {grp} on {date} was {scc} thousand per ml. Please test the suspect cows, milk them last and keep their milk out of the tank until we know more.
Hello {keeper}, {section} gave {eggs} eggs from {hens} hens on {date}, a lay rate of {lay_rate}. Please check feed, water, light and signs of stress or disease in the house and tell me today.
Hello {keeper}, the cracked share in {section} was {crack_pct} ({cracked} eggs) on {date}. Please check the belts, the nest pads and the handling and tell me what you change.
Hello {keeper}, {name} holds {content_t} tonnes of {product} and is {pct_full} full with {space_t} tonnes of space left. Please plan where the next lots go.
Store keeper: moisture high in a bin
Hello {keeper}, the moisture of {product} in {name} is {moisture}. The check shows: {moist_state}. Please run the fan, turn the grain and tell me whether it needs drying.
Hello {keeper}, {name} reads {temp_now} degrees C and must stay between {tmin} and {tmax}. The check shows: {state}. Please check the unit, the door seal and the stock and call me.
Store keeper: lot ready for dispatch
Hello, lot {lot_id} ({crop}, {tonnes} tonnes) from {field} is in {store} and ready for dispatch. Please prepare the load, the lot label and the delivery note.
Hello {counter}, the count of {product} on {date} shows {counted_t} tonnes against {book_t} in the book, a difference of {diff_t} tonnes. Please count again and check the movement records.
Hello {found_by}, thank you for reporting spoilage in lot {lot}: {tonnes} tonnes of {product}, cause {cause}. Please separate the affected stock, clean the area and send photos.
Store keeper: crates short for tomorrow
Hello {packed_by}, tomorrow we pack {product} for {buyer}, about {crates} crates of {crate_kg} kg. Please count the clean crates today and tell me if we are short.
Hello, drying of lot {lot} ({crop}, {tonnes_in} tonnes) is booked on {date}, from {moist_in} down to {moist_out}. {operator} runs the dryer. Please confirm the storage space and the lot label.
